text: Some emails are long, and the one thing they ask of you is buried in the middle. If you cannot skim, because of dyslexia, low vision, or because you cannot rely on sound, finding that request means reading everything again and again.

Jeri, by team FullStuckEngineer, does not just summarise. It finds what the email asks of you, shows the evidence, checks the dates, and leaves the decision to you. This is the live app, using a fictional example email.

We open an interview invitation from Northbridge, a fictional company. Gemini reads the email once. While it works, the page shows where each answer will appear. This wait is real, and shortened here.
Here is the result. What the email is. Your ask: confirm the interview, or propose two other times, using their form. And below it, the exact sentences from the email that support it.

Now the part a summary would miss. Our code, not the AI, checks every date. The email says Wednesday the twelfth of November, but that date is a Thursday. The deadline is written as Thursday the thirteenth, which is a Friday, and it falls after the interview. Jeri does not guess which day is right. It shows what the email says, what the check found, and links each warning to the original sentence.
There are three ways to take this in, all from the same analysis. Listen reads short spoken beats aloud. It never plays by itself.
Switch to Captions. The audio stops, and the same sentence appears as text, in the same place. No sound is needed.
Easy Read shows large, plain cards, one topic each. Every 'not' is kept. For example: you do not need your residence card for the video call.

At the bottom, the Draft Dock holds a reply that asks which day they mean, instead of confirming a date that may be wrong. Approve records your decision: approved, not sent. Jeri never sends email. And if you edit the draft, the approval is cleared.

Under the hood, Gemini analyses the email once, into a structured result. Our code verifies the quotes and the dates. Gemini text to speech provides the voice. Results are saved, so switching modes never calls the AI again. Gmail sign-in is built, but not connected in this demo, so it uses a built-in inbox of fictional emails.
Jeri finds the ask, keeps the meaning, and lets you choose the next step. Jeri, by FullStuckEngineer.
